concepts.title: Indus Valley or Harappan Civilisation Overview

questions.q: Using the method 'Indus Valley or Harappan Civilisation Overview', work with: end_year = 100, start_year = 200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of duration.
questions.a: 100 times

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Indus Valley or Harappan Civilisation Overview' and work with: end_year = 200, start_year = 1000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of duration.
questions.a: 800 times

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Indus Valley or Harappan Civilisation Overview' refers to.
questions.a: The Harappan Civilisation flourished in the Indus valley from about 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE, making it one of the earliest urban civilizations of the world.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Indus Valley or Harappan Civilisation Overview'.
questions.a: The Harappan Civilisation was a Bronze Age urban culture spread across north-western India and present-day Pakistan, known for its planned cities.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Indus Valley or Harappan Civilisation Overview', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: duration = end_year - start_year

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Town Planning and Drainage' refers to.
questions.a: Harappan cities were carefully planned with a grid of streets, rectangular houses of baked bricks, and an advanced covered drainage system.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Town Planning and Drainage'.
questions.a: The systematic town planning and drainage of Harappan cities show a high level of civic organisation and engineering skill.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Town Planning and Drainage'.
questions.a: describe the town planning of Harappan cities

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Great Bath and Granaries' refers to.
questions.a: The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro was a large waterproof tank probably used for ritual bathing, while granaries were large storehouses for surplus grain.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Great Bath and Granaries'.
questions.a: Public structures like the Great Bath and granaries reveal the importance of religion, hygiene, and food storage in Harappan society.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'The Great Bath and Granaries'.
questions.a: describe the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Agriculture and Trade' refers to.
questions.a: The Harappans practised agriculture along the fertile Indus floodplains and carried out extensive trade with regions within and beyond the subcontinent.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Agriculture and Trade'.
questions.a: Surplus agricultural production supported urban life and enabled the Harappans to trade goods such as beads, cotton, and metals over long distances.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Agriculture and Trade'.
questions.a: describe the agriculture of the Harappan civilisation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Arts and Crafts' refers to.
questions.a: The Harappans were skilled artisans who produced beads, pottery, jewellery, metal tools, and figurines, showing advanced craft techniques.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Arts and Crafts'.
questions.a: Specialised crafts such as bead-making, pottery, and metalworking reflect a prosperous and technologically skilled Harappan society.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Arts and Crafts'.
questions.a: describe the arts and crafts of the Harappan civilisation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Seals and Writing' refers to.
questions.a: Harappan seals, usually made of steatite, carry engravings of animals and a script that has not yet been fully deciphered.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Seals and Writing'.
questions.a: The seals were likely used for trade and identification, and the undeciphered script points to a literate Harappan society.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Seals and Writing'.
questions.a: describe the seals of the Harappan civilisation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Decline of the Harappan Civilisation' refers to.
questions.a: The Harappan Civilisation declined around 1900 BCE, possibly due to a combination of climate change, drying of rivers, floods, and a decline in trade.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Decline of the Harappan Civilisation'.
questions.a: The decline of the Harappan cities was gradual and may have resulted from environmental changes and economic factors rather than a single invasion.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Decline of the Harappan Civilisation'.
questions.a: explain the possible causes of the decline of the Harappan civilisation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Legacy of the Harappan Civilisation' refers to.
questions.a: The Harappan Civilisation left a lasting legacy in town planning, crafts, agricultural practices, and cultural traditions that influenced later Indian civilization.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Legacy of the Harappan Civilisation'.
questions.a: Many elements of Harappan culture, such as planned settlements, craft traditions, and symbols, continued in later periods of Indian history.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Legacy of the Harappan Civilisation'.
questions.a: describe the legacy of the Harappan civilisation
